pos.personaBrief: Menotti's sides used the ball as the engine (El Gráfico 1978: the ball moved the team and cut risk) with reasoned possession and sudden verticality at Huracán; he never ceded the ball on purpose.

pro.personaBrief: Huracán combined tight triangles and first-touch play with sudden verticalizations; Menotti wanted precision first, then speed, and a 4-3-3 with direct runners, so he built up with intent rather than going long.

est.personaBrief: Menotti demanded permanent mobility and a close, combining circulation, but kept wingers wide (Bertoni and Ortiz bien abiertos) and a clear cinco, so a relational team with some defined roles.

lar.personaBrief: He kept wide forwards and wingers like Houseman and Larrosa running the flanks, while full-backs were not meant to go forward (1973 interview), and in 1978 Argentina played a 4-3-3 with wide forwards.

blo.personaBrief: Huracán aimed to win the ball as close to the opposition goal as possible, and Argentina 1978 stood very high, pressed with achique and led the World Cup in recoveries (55 per match, 11 in under six seconds).

mar.personaBrief: Menotti said his team marked en zona like Brazil in its three titles, recovering the ball through occupation of space, and rejected man-marking as the Zubeldia/Bilardo school.

pla.personaBrief: Menotti said his main concern was his players' fundamentals, the opponent interested but did not worry him; he imposed a style and played the same final against the Dutch as throughout, with the aim of winning by playing well.

res.personaBrief: He wanted to win by playing well as long-range policy, disdained winning 1-0 from a free kick, and said there are many ways to win but his was the lyrical one; the game was about spectacle with results too.

sis.personaBrief: He gave talent 100 percent importance and picked technically gifted players, but demanded discipline and work and left out Maradona; the plan was his, so talent inside a collective plan.

jog.personaBrief: Talent got 100 percent importance (1973) and the team was chosen for technical ability (Ardiles, Houseman), though he stressed intensity and fitness to match the Europeans and the cinco was a ball-winner who also passed.

bas.personaBrief: He promoted decades of players from the interior and youth sides (Toulon 1975, Youth World Cup 1979), but for the 1978 World Cup he chose experience over Maradona and relied on veterans like Fillol and Passarella.

lid.personaBrief: He rejected imposed discipline as a military regime and wanted honest people, convictions shared by the group, yet he fixed the plan himself and cut Maradona and Gatti without concession.
